chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to the Clan of Salima: 'O Clan of Salima, who is your master and leader?' They replied, 'O Messenger of Allah, our chief is a man who is stingy.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) then said, 'And what illness is more severe than stinginess?' Then he said, 'Rather, your chief is the one with the white body, Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about stinginess being a severe illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the Shia distinction between social status and spiritual virtue, where the Prophet (peace be upon him) contrasts the common perception of leadership with true nobility. By identifying Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur as the true 'Sayyid' despite the clan's focus on a stingy figure, the narration emphasizes that character, not just lineage or wealth, defines leadership. This aligns with the broader Islamic principle that stinginess is a spiritual disease that corrupts the soul, a theme frequently echoed in Quranic exegesis.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Ahmad, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said to the Clan of Salima: ‘O banu Salmah, who is your master and leader?’ They replied, ‘O Messenger of Allahsaww, our chief is a stingy man.’ The Messenger of Allahsaww then said, ‘No illness is more serious than stinginess.’ He then said, ‘In fact, your chief is al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur, whose body is white..
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once asked banu Salmah, ‘O banu Salmah, who is your master and leader?’ They replied, ‘O Messenger of Allah, our chief is a stingy man.’ The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘No illness is more serious than stinginess.’ He then said, ‘In fact, your chief is al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur, whose body is white.’”
